channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Tailoring Resistance Exercise for Knee Osteoarthritis: An Intervention Systematic Review With Dose-Response Meta-analysis of the Effects of Intensity and Volume.
item.description: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of RCTs found dose-response relationships between isotonic lower extremity resistance exercise volume and outcomes of pain, function, and strength in people with knee osteoarthritis (OA), and compared different intensities and delivery methods.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Efficacy of Exercise Therapy for Nonspecific Chronic Low Back Pain According to the FITT Principle: A Systematic Review With Meta-analyses.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analyses evaluated the efficacy of exercise therapy interventions, differing in frequency, intensity, type, and time (FITT), on disability in individuals with nonspecific chronic low back pain (LBP).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Biofeedback in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analysis found that biofeedback added to practice significantly improves lower limb activity in individuals with Parkinson's disease compared to practice alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Carrying an unseen weight: the neuro-perceptual landscape of limb heaviness after stroke- a scoping review.
item.description: A scoping review identified perceived limb heaviness as an under-recognized stroke symptom, often unrelated to weakness or spasticity. Proposed mechanisms include altered sensorimotor integration, impaired proprioception, and disrupted body representation, suggesting issues in sensorimotor processing.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: White Matter Diffusion Anisotropy and the Effects of Inpatient Multidisciplinary Rehabilitation in Parkinson's Disease: A Diffusion Tensor Imaging Analysis.
item.description: A diffusion tensor imaging analysis found that pretreatment corticospinal tract fractional anisotropy predicted responsiveness to an 8-week inpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation program in 94 Parkinson's disease patients, with responders showing significant UPDRS Part III improvement.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Aquatic Tai Chi and Computer Assisted Rehabilitation Environment-Based Virtual Reality Training on Rehabilitation in Patients with Parkinson Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blind RCT with 50 Parkinson's disease patients (Hoehn-Yahr stage 2-3) compared 12 weeks of aquatic Tai Chi (n=26) versus Computer Assisted Rehabilitation Environment-based virtual reality training (n=24). Both interventions led to improvements in UPDRS-III, BBS, TUG, and 6-minute walk test.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department (RESHAP-ED): a randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation.
item.description: The RESHAP-ED pragmatic RCT evaluated physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in five Australian emergency departments, demonstrating improved effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness compared to usual care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Focal Muscle Vibration for Upper Limb Spasticity After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies (inception-March 2026) involving adults with post-stroke upper limb spasticity found focal muscle vibration (FMV) has a significant effect (Hedges' g=0.74, 95% CI 0.52-0.97) on reducing spasticity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Arm exercise training in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
item.description: An umbrella review synthesizing findings from six databases found that arm exercise training is a key component of pulmonary rehabilitation for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), addressing extrapulmonary features and improving functional outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Application of non-invasive electroencephalogram-based brain-computer interfaces in post-stroke hand function rehabilitation.
item.description: This article reviews the application of non-invasive EEG-based brain-computer interfaces (BCI) for post-stroke hand function rehabilitation. BCI decodes imagined hand movements to drive exoskeletons, FES, or VR devices, aiming to remodel neural pathways and promote motor recovery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Development and psychometric validation of the shoulder problems assessment scale.
item.description: This multicenter study developed and validated the 12-item Shoulder Problems Assessment Scale (SPAS), an activity-based patient-reported outcome measure using a hierarchical stepwise yes/no format, with field testing on n = 415 patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Prestroke Rehabilitation Reserve and Mobility and Self-Care Outcomes After Incident Stroke Across Four International Aging Cohorts.
item.description: A harmonized longitudinal cohort study (N=7486, mean age 70.0 years) across four international aging cohorts found that lower multidimensional pre-stroke rehabilitation reserve was associated with adverse mobility and self-care status after incident stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of high-intensity laser therapy and extracorporeal shock wave therapy for the treatment of plantar flexor spasticity in post-stroke patients.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial with 42 stroke patients compared high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) and radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) as adjunctive treatments for plantar flexor spasticity, with both groups showing greater improvements than rehabilitation alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effectiveness of instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization on pain and function in patients with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (n=550) found that instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization (IASTM) significantly improved pain (SMD -0.74; 95% CI -1.04 to -0.44) and function (SMD -0.66; 95% CI -0.99 to -0.34) in musculoskeletal disorders in the short term, with moderate effect sizes.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Exploring animal-assisted therapy in stroke rehabilitation: a systematic review of emerging evidence.
item.description: A systematic review of 12 studies on animal-assisted therapy (AAT) in adult stroke rehabilitation found emerging evidence primarily for psychosocial and emotional benefits, with limited data on motor or cognitive outcomes due to varied study designs and small sample sizes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Therapeutic Exercise Protocol During Hospitalization in Pediatric Oncohematological Patients: Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial involving 30 pediatric oncohematological patients (8-17 years) demonstrated that a therapeutic exercise program during hospitalization improved quality of life, muscle strength, and functional capacity compared to a minimal active physiotherapy comparator.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Musculoskeletal impairments associated with migraine in young adults: a case-control study.
item.description: A case-control study involving 140 university students found associations between migraine and musculoskeletal impairments, including core and cervical muscle endurance, and craniovertebral angle.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Minimal Important Changes in Accelerometer-Measured Physical Activity and Sedentary Time in Older Patients With Subacute Stroke: A Multicenter Study.
item.description: A multicenter observational study involving 299 subacute stroke patients estimated the minimal important change (MIC) for accelerometer-measured sedentary behavior, light-intensity physical activity, and moderate-to-vigorous intensity physical activity, ranging from 11.4 to 34.2 minutes, based on improvements in FIM scores.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Feasibility, content and construct validity of the Patient Specific Functional Scale for chronic stroke survivors.
item.description: A cross-sectional study with 66 chronic stroke survivors (median 81 years old, 76 months post-onset) confirmed the feasibility, content validity, and construct validity of the Patient Specific Functional Scale (PSFS) using COSMIN standards, with high completion rates and good correlation to other functional measures.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A domain-specific approach to characterizing balance confidence post-stroke.
item.description: A cross-sectional analysis confirmed that the Activities-Specific Balance Confidence (ABC) scale consists of three factors—anticipatory control, walking balance, and reactive balance—in 248 community-dwelling adults with chronic stroke.
item.author: PubMed
